HUJI Indoor Navigation

Find your way across Mount Scopus.

Maze is designed to help students and visitors navigate the Hebrew University Mount Scopus campus from campus entrances to buildings, classrooms, offices, elevators, stairs and facilities. For the current beta, the working indoor navigation supports Building 21.

Start navigation Contact us

Why we built Maze

Mount Scopus can be difficult to navigate for new students and visitors: many buildings, several entrances, multi-floor layouts, similar corridors and room numbers that are hard to understand at first. Maze was built as a browser-based campus guide. Our goal is to support the entire campus, and for the current beta we focused on Building 21 to create a working navigation algorithm.

Less confusionClear left/right directions instead of technical map language.
Campus-wide visionDesigned for the full Mount Scopus campus, starting with Building 21.
Building 21 betaThe current working algorithm supports floors, stairs, elevators and rooms in Building 21.
No app neededOpen the webpage, choose a supported destination, and start walking.

First get to campus

Use your favorite navigation app to reach the Mount Scopus campus entrance. Once you arrive, use Maze for the supported indoor route inside Building 21 while we continue expanding the app to the full campus.

Google Maps Waze Moovit
Campus vision

Today Building 21. Tomorrow the full Mount Scopus campus.

Maze was designed as a campus wide indoor navigation platform for Hebrew University. The long term goal is to help people move from any campus entrance to any building, room or facility. For this version, we focused on Building 21 so we could build a working algorithm and a real navigation experience.

Campus buildings Future versions can support more buildings across Mount Scopus, not only Building 21.
Rooms and facilities The product vision includes classrooms, offices, elevators, stairs, restrooms, libraries and student services.
Smarter routes The goal is to support simple, accessible and multi floor routes that feel natural to follow.

How Maze fits into the trip

Use the apps you already know to arrive at campus. Then Maze takes over and guides you indoors to the exact room.

Contact us

Maze is a student project built to make indoor navigation across the Mount Scopus campus easier for new students, guests and staff. The current beta supports Building 21 only. For feedback, bugs, missing rooms or route corrections, contact the project team.
